gloss: to have · there is · being — and, in Buddhist texts, becoming (bhava)
formNote: Bronze forms show a hand holding a piece of meat, which is commonly read as “to hold, to have”. The Shuowen instead analyses the graph as 月 (moon) with 又 as phonetic. Mojidata IDS describes the modern graph as ⿸𠂇月.
summary: To have, and there is: Chinese uses one word for possession and existence. In the Daodejing 有 pairs with 無 as being and non-being; in Buddhist translation it renders bhava, “becoming”, the tenth of the twelve links.
placement: On the left of the sphere, below its equator, facing the reader: being on one side of the hollow axis. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: Becoming, in the Twelve Links
satellites.evidence: In the twelve links of dependent arising, 有 renders bhava, “becoming” or “existence”, between grasping (取, upādāna) and birth (生, jāti). It comes two links after 愛 (tṛṣṇā), so the Pillars’ 愛 and the Ground’s 有 stand in the same chain.
satellites.caveat: Bhava is coming-to-be, not possession; the translators chose 有 for its existential sense, “there is”.

satellites.title: A Hand Holding Meat
satellites.evidence: In bronze inscriptions the graph is a right hand (又) holding meat (肉, later written like 月), a picture of having or holding. The Shuowen, working from seal script, took the lower part as 月 “moon” and 又 as the sound.
satellites.caveat: The hand-and-meat reading is the common modern one; the Shuowen’s analysis differs, and the two should not be merged.
gaps: Name a modern palaeographic source for the hand-and-meat reading.
